finding.rationale: The source explicitly resolves the recorded acknowledgement from superseded 15:20 to correct 15:02 and says that the draft correction was completed. B does more than ask an open confirmation question: its suggestion first questions the recorded acknowledgement time, then asserts that the actual time is not confirmed. Its matching question expressly reopens whether the recorded time is still unconfirmed. Together these undo the supplied correction, so the frozen instruction against ignoring an explicit correction applies even though the sentence appears in a suggestion.
finding.counter_reading_considered: A mailbox timestamp need not establish every conceivable physical sub-event, and a hypothetical question alone could seek permissible additional confirmation. Here neither the source nor B distinguishes a separate sending, receipt, or physical sub-event; B expressly calls the already corrected recorded acknowledgement time into doubt. Inventing that distinction to reinterpret the output would exceed the text. The finding is narrowly about reopening the supplied recorded-time status.
finding.limits: This does not assert that B invented a replacement timestamp, restored 15:20 as fact, or claimed a completed event. It is one stale-status error, not a second error for the repeated confirmation question.
